mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a four-week monotonic narrowing of its deficit from -39.0 to -28.7, indicating an underlying recovery momentum that is expected to persist and push mean RETAIL_REC higher over the next 28 days relative to the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise further (flattens or reverses) in more than half of comparable continuation windows after four consecutive weeks of improvement.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week drop in TRANSIT of more than 1.5 points combined with a simultaneous drop in WORKPLACES signals renewed mobility restrictions or voluntary avoidance that will suppress retail footfall over the following two weeks, lowering RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 1.5 points week-on-week AND WORKPLACES falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -37.0 to -38.6 and WORKPLACES fell from -30.9 to -34.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise or stays flat despite the joint TRANSIT and WORKPLACES decline observed at t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained improvement in GROCERY_PHARM (from -8.3 to -2.4) reflects declining precautionary stockpiling and growing comfort with in-person errands, a behavioral shift that is expected to spill over into increased discretionary retail visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved each week from -8.3 to -2.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise even though GROCERY_PHARM continues its upward trend over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Continued improvement in PARKS (from -45.7 to -28.9) indicates increasing outdoor leisure activity that substitutes for indoor retail and recreation visits, exerting a seasonal drag that lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -45.7 to -28.9 over four weeks while RETAIL_REC improvement decelerated
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in tandem with PARKS rather than being suppressed by it, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility ticking upward (22.9 to 24.3) alongside stalling RETAIL_REC improvement (-29.1 to -28.7) suggests a renewed preference for staying home, which will slow or reverse the RETAIL_REC recovery over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises week-on-week while RETAIL_REC improvement rate falls below 1 point
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 22.9 to 24.3 while RETAIL_REC improvement slowed to 0.4 points at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to improve at a similar or faster pace despite RESIDENTIAL rising.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility drops by more than 3 points in a single week, it signals a disruption to commuting-linked retail visits (e.g., lunch, after-work shopping), which will reduce RETAIL_REC over the subsequent two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -30.9 to -34.6, a 3.7 point drop, at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the two weeks following a WORKPLACES drop exceeding 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of partial reopening where TRANSIT remains persistently more negative than WORKPLACES and RETAIL_REC (as seen at t-0w), transit-dependent retail access remains constrained, capping any further RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -38.6 is more negative than both WORKPLACES (-34.6) and RETAIL_REC (-28.7) at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises substantially over the next four weeks even though TRANSIT remains the most depressed series relative to WORKPLACES and RETAIL_REC.

mechanism_narrative: The deceleration in RETAIL_REC's week-on-week improvement (from +7.0 points at t-2w to +0.4 points at t-0w) indicates the recovery is losing momentum and approaching a plateau, implying the next week will show flat or slightly negative RETAIL_REC movement.
candidate_trigger: week-on-week RETAIL_REC improvement falls below 1 point for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly gains shrank from 7.0 to 2.9 to 0.4 points across the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC resumes a gain of more than 2 points in the next week despite the observed deceleration pattern.
